Operator: Good day, and welcome to the TeleMedia Corp Q2 Earnings Conference Call. All participants are currently in a listen-only mode. After the speakers' presentation, there will be a question-and-answer session. Instructions for those joining by phone: If you're using a speakerphone, please pick up your handset to minimize background noise. As a reminder, this conference is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the call over to Sarah Thompson, Head of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Sarah Thompson: Thank you, Operator. Good morning, everyone, and welcome to TeleMedia Corp's Q2 Earnings Conference Call. Joining me on the call today are Mike Reynolds, Chief Executive Officer; Lisa Chen, Chief Financial Officer; and other members of our leadership team.

Before we begin, I would like to remind you that today's discussion may contain forward-looking statements. These statements are based on management's current expectations and are subject to risks and uncertainties that could cause actual results to differ materially. Please refer to our SEC filings for a more complete discussion of these risks.

Mike Reynolds: Thank you, Sarah, and good morning, everyone. I'm pleased to report our results for Q2. We achieved significant progress in our fiber buildout, expanding coverage and accelerating customer adoption, which reflects our strong execution in a dynamic market. We are particularly excited about the initial performance of our TeleStream+ service and its seamless integration with high-speed connectivity, driving robust uptake across our bundles. Our investments in spectrum assets are also paying off, with improved utilization enhancing capacity for 5G and media delivery. Furthermore, we have focused on optimizing ARPU through strategic pricing and bundling, which has allowed us to maintain profitability while growing revenue per user. Finally, our strategic focus remains on dividend sustainability and delivering strong shareholder returns.

Lisa Chen: Thank you, Mike. Turning to the financials, our revenue for the quarter was $15.2 billion, representing a 6% increase year-over-year. Our adjusted EBITDA was $5.5 billion, with a margin of 36.2%. We continue to manage our expenses effectively and are on track to meet our financial targets for the year. Our capital expenditures were $4.0 billion, primarily driven by investments in our 5G network expansion and fiber deployments.

Good afternoon, everyone—let me now dive deeper into some key areas starting with our fiber buildout, which remains the cornerstone of our long-term growth strategy across telecommunications and media. Our Fiber to the Home network is essential for providing multi-gig symmetrical speeds, not only for superior broadband but also for smooth integration with media streaming bundles like our own TeleStream+ and partnerships with services such as Disney+, Netflix, and Peacock. Demand is surging due to ongoing cord-cutting, sustained remote work, and the rise in 8K streaming and cloud gaming, where sub-10ms latency is now essential.

On the key metrics for Q2, we reached 8.2 million homes passed with fiber, a 25% increase from 6.6 million at the end of Q2 last year, including a record sequential addition of 1.1 million homes passed from Q1. This keeps us on pace for our full-year target of 11 to 12 million homes passed by year-end. For subscribers, we hit 2.9 million fiber broadband customers, up 18% year-over-year with 320,000 net adds sequentially. This translates to a penetration rate of 35.4% of homes passed, improving 250 basis points from the prior quarter and accelerating from 30% a year ago.

Regionally, our Sunbelt areas—Florida, Texas, and the Carolinas—are leading the charge, representing 55% of new homes passed this quarter. In Florida, we laid more than 2,500 route miles of fiber, reaching 450,000 additional homes in growing markets like Tampa and Orlando, where housing starts rose 15% year-over-year according to Census figures. Take rates there reached 42%, boosted by bundling 2Gig fiber plans at $120 per month with TeleStream+ for an extra $10, pushing blended ARPU for these fiber customers to $142, up 7% from last year. In Northeast urban areas like Philadelphia and Boston, we added 300,000 homes passed with more deliberate pacing, but achieved top-tier take rates of 48% through dense builds and monthly churn of just 0.9%, far below the industry average of 1.4% as noted by New Street Research.

For rural and suburban pushes, we're tapping into federal programs like the $42.5 billion BEAD initiative and our $1.2 billion RDOF commitment from 2021. We've lit up fiber in 15 Midwest rural counties, passing 150,000 homes using GPON overlays on existing infrastructure at a reduced cost per home passed of $850—20% lower than last year thanks to better trenching and micro-trenching methods. Adoption is building to a 22% take rate, with starting ARPU at $110 on 1Gig plans, and strong media cross-sells—65% of new rural fiber subscribers chose our Entertainment 300 bundle featuring ad-supported Paramount+ and local sports streaming.

On the technical front, we're outpacing our XGS-PON upgrade schedule, with over 70% of new builds now supporting 10G symmetrical speeds, and 50G PON pilots running in Atlanta with Nokia. This gives us an advantage over cable competitors like Comcast's DOCSIS 4.0, which remains asymmetric at 40G down and 10G up. We've also virtualized OLTs and integrated with our 5G fixed wireless access mid-split, delivering 85% fiber-like throughput in hybrid zones to improve low-density economics.

This expansion is reshaping our financials: fiber EBITDA margins now top 55%, compared to 42% on legacy hybrid fiber-coax networks, and we're capturing $300 million in yearly capex savings from dark fiber leases to enterprise clients like AWS Direct Connect. Lifetime value for fiber customers is 2.5 times higher than legacy, with payback periods under 24 months at these take rates. Competition is intense—Verizon Fios holds strong in the Northeast—but our media bundles deliver a 15-point NPS advantage per JD Power surveys. Satellite options like Starlink remain limited to niches, with urban penetration below 5% per FCC stats.

Moving ahead, we'll ramp to 1.5 million homes passed per quarter in the second half, aiming for 40% take rates by year-end via focused marketing and $50 monthly intro offers on 1Gig service. Expect quarterly subscriber adds at a 450,000 run-rate, with fiber revenue up 28% year-over-year. Full-year capex holds at $4.2 to 4.5 billion, with 75% directed to fiber. We're eyeing tuck-in deals, such as our $250 million purchase of a 200,000-home Florida incumbent local exchange carrier, and more BEAD Phase 2 opportunities.

Now, shifting to ARPU trends, which are proving to be a key engine for revenue expansion in this competitive telecom and media environment. ARPU serves as our core measure for extracting value from our roughly 185 million global subscribers spanning mobile, fixed broadband, and bundled media. In Q2, blended ARPU hit $58.42, a solid 6.2% year-over-year rise from $55.01—a $3.41 gain highlighting our pricing discipline and bundling innovations.

By segment, postpaid wireless service ARPU reached $49.27, up 4.8% or $2.25 year-over-year. This stemmed from a 3% mid-quarter hike on Unlimited plans in North America starting in Q1, plus 5% increases on premium 5G Ultra tiers in Europe, where demand elasticity stayed under 1% amid high-usage patterns. Bundles like '5G Everywhere + StreamMax'—pairing unlimited 5G with our ad-supported StreamMax video service—added 1.5 percentage points to the growth. These now reach 42% of postpaid mobile users, up from 28% last year, contributing about $1.20 extra per user from media upsells.

In fixed broadband, ARPU climbed to $68.75, an 8.1% increase or $5.14 gain. We rolled out 4-6% hikes on gigabit tiers in the U.S. and Asia-Pacific, backed by FTTH coverage now at 55% of our U.S. service area, matching AT&T's pace. The 'Xtend Home' bundle—1Gbps fiber plus mobile and StreamMax at 15% off standalone prices—drove 38% of new broadband adds, adding 3.2 percentage points to ARPU as users upgrade from DOCSIS 3.1 cable for better gaming and 8K performance. In Europe, facing Digital Markets Act constraints, we used bundles with local content like Premier League access to secure 5.2% growth.

Media video ARPU stood at $14.62, up 7.9% or $1.07, with bundling pushing attach rates to 65% across mobile and broadband, similar to Comcast's approach but leveraged globally. Promotions like 'Family Unlimited' with four StreamMax streams and controls countered cord-cutting, as U.S. pay-TV homes fell 3% per Nielsen.

Geographically, North America topped with 7.5% blended growth to $62.10, aided by 5G standalone upgrades boosting data use by 25% and enabling $2 monthly hotspot add-ons. Europe grew 4.1% to $54.80 despite UK price caps, stabilized by MVNO deals like Virgin Media O2 equivalents. Emerging markets in Latin America and APAC saw 9.2% to $42.35 via affordable bundles, such as 20GB 4G plus basic StreamMax for $8 monthly in Brazil, alongside 5G NR tests.

Under our 'ValueMax' approach, we price based on network value, avoiding commoditization. Open RAN in 15 markets trimmed opex 18%, supporting capex for C-band wins like our $2.2 billion for 140MHz in the U.S. Bundled customer lifetime value is 2.3 times standalone, with quarterly churn at 1.1%, down 45 basis points.

For Q3, we anticipate 5-7% blended ARPU growth from 3-5% pricing in core markets and new StreamMax + Apple TV+ bundles. Churn holds at 0.95%, and we'll track rivals like T-Mobile's Go5G Next and Charter's mobile moves, setting up mid-single-digit revenue growth in FY24.

Next, let's discuss our spectrum assets, utilization rates, and plans for future deployment—a critical foundation for our wireless and media convergence serving 45 million postpaid mobile lines and 30 million fixed wireless access homes under our "Connect Everywhere" vision. We hold about 1.2 million MHz-POPs nationally, with 145 MHz average depth in the top 100 markets, rivaling T-Mobile and Verizon. Breakdown: 25% low-band (600 and 850 MHz) for coverage, 55% mid-band (C-band 3.7-4.2 GHz and refarmed 2.5 GHz PCS), and 20% mmWave (26 and 39 GHz) for urban capacity. Acquired via $8.2 billion in the 2021 C-band auction and refarming.

Utilization averages 72% nationally during peak hours (7-11 PM ET), up 14% year-over-year and 8% sequentially, tracked by throughput per MHz, bits per Hz, and efficiency metrics. Mid-band leads at 78% via 5G aggregation like n71 + n41 + n77. Low-band at 65% supports off-peak IoT/NB-IoT, while mmWave hits 82% in stadiums and data centers with beamforming and 64T64R MIMO.

Drivers include 5G data at 18 GB monthly per postpaid user (up 22%), from NovaStream app edge caching on O-RAN radios; 1.2 million FWA adds using mid-band for 500 Mbps+ in suburbs against AT&T Fiber; and 30% CBRS growth for enterprise AR/VR media with Disney and NBCUniversal. This supports 5% ARPU to $58.40 and postpaid churn under 0.5%.

Regionally, Northeast Corridor (25% POPs) at 81% from urban demand, refarming AWS-3 LTE to 5G for 2.5x efficiency. Rural Midwest/Southeast at 58%, using low-band and LEO backhaul like AST SpaceMobile. California/Texas mmWave over 85% for "Media Edge" low-latency sports streaming vs. YouTube TV.

Forward plans allocate $4.8 billion of $12 billion FY24 wireless capex to optimization: refarm 20 MHz 850 MHz to 5G n5 by mid-2025 for 15% capacity; DSS live in 60 markets pushing C-band to 85%; bid $2-3 billion in CBRS expansion and mmWave auctions for 100 MHz mid-band; $500 million Open RAN with Nokia/Samsung for AI orchestration, 20% efficiency by 2026; 10% C-band slicing for ad-tech latency cuts; 5% low-band for 988 Lifeline; BEAD hybrids for 90% 100/20 Mbps rural coverage by 2027.

This fuels bundled moats like 5G home + Peacock-style streaming at 12% cross-sell, with 3.2x leverage and $2.5 billion FCF covering growth amid interference risks.

Finally, on dividend sustainability and shareholder returns, as we build momentum, our capital discipline stands out amid 5G/fiber spending and streaming challenges. We returned $10.7 billion to shareholders in the first half via dividends and buybacks—up 12% from prior periods—while fortifying our balance sheet.

Our quarterly dividend is $0.55 per share, annualizing to $2.20, the 17th straight increase, yielding 4.8% forward versus peers' 3.9% for Verizon, AT&T, Comcast. Payout at 58% of adjusted EPS $3.78 (up 8% on wireless ARPU and media ads), down from 62%.

Free cash flow of $9.2 billion annualized exceeds guidance by $400 million from opex savings and subs, covering $4.8 billion dividends at 192%—top-quartile 9.1% levered FCF yield per Bloomberg.

Capex peaked at $14.5 billion last year (18% revenue) for C-Band/FTTH; now guiding $13.2 billion in FY24 (-9%) as 85% footprint is 5G Ultra Wideband. $750 million synergies from SpectrumCo deal.

Leverage at 2.4x net debt/EBITDA (from 2.8x), refinanced $3 billion sub-4%, $15 billion undrawn revolver for bolt-ons against Starlink.

U.S. core (75% EBITDA) drives with 1.2 million broadband/850k phone adds via fixed-mobile bundles. Europe Vodafone JV $1.1 billion FCF, 45% 5G vs. EU 32%; Asia-Pacific Singtel/Jio royalties $500 million from FAST channels.

$6 billion buyback auth, $3.9 billion executed 8% below NAV; total yield 11.2% vs. S&P Telecom 7.8%. Guide $11.5-12.5 billion returns FY24, 5-7% dividend growth on 3-5% FCF from AI orchestration (15% RAN opex cut) and 25% CTV ad utilization.

Stress-tested to 20% ARPU drop, coverage >140%. Our model de-risks dividends.

Operator: Thank you. We will now begin the question-and-answer session. Instructions for Q&A: Ask one question and one follow-up. Our first question comes from David Lee with Morningstar. Please go ahead.

David Lee: Good morning. Can you provide more color on the competitive dynamics around your fiber take rates and how bundling is differentiating you?

Mike Reynolds: Certainly, David. Our media integration, like TeleStream+ bundles, is key—giving us that NPS edge and higher ARPU as we expand in Sunbelt and rural areas. Take rates are accelerating as payback shortens, positioning us ahead of pure-play fiber rivals.

Operator: Our next question comes from Emily Carter with Barclays. Please go ahead.

Emily Carter: Hi, thanks. Could you elaborate on your plans for spectrum allocation in light of upcoming auctions and FWA growth?

Lisa Chen: Yes, Emily. We're prioritizing mid-band via CBRS and mmWave bids, with refarming and DSS boosting utilization to support FWA adds. This aligns with our $4.8 billion wireless capex, enhancing bundled media delivery and capacity for data surges.

Sarah Thompson: Thank you for your questions. That concludes our Q&A session. Mike, would you like to provide closing remarks?

Mike Reynolds: Thank you. In closing, I am proud of our team's performance this quarter. We are well-positioned to continue delivering value to our customers and shareholders. Thank you for joining us today.

Operator: This concludes today's conference call. Thank you for your participation. You may now disconnect.
